strengths: Clear problem motivation: Effectively identifies and articulates the challenge of negative guidance in few-step models with specific limitations of prior work (CFG, NASA, NAG)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple baselines, trade-off analysis, ablation studies, and computational cost measurements demonstrate thorough empirical investigation
Simple and practical method: VSF is elegant, easy to implement, and requires minimal computational overhead compared to traditional CFG
Better trade-off curves: Figure 8 demonstrates VSF achieves superior positive-negative prompt adherence trade-offs compared to main baselines (NAG, NASA)
Computational efficiency: Faster than CFG while maintaining competitive quality, with detailed runtime measurements provided
weaknesses: Critical evaluation limitation - No human evaluation: For an image generation paper claiming quality and concept removal improvements, the absence of human evaluation is a major gap, especially given acknowledged MLLM unreliability

MLLM evaluation concerns: The paper explicitly acknowledges (Section 4.3, Figure 6) that MLLM metrics are unreliable with examples showing 70-point scores for heavily distorted images, yet this is the primary quantitative evaluation metric
Limited technical novelty: The core contribution of sign-flipping attention values is an incremental modification of existing negative guidance methods (NAG, NASA) without fundamentally new insights
Insufficient theoretical justification: Equation 6 and the claim about attention ratio equivalence lack rigorous derivation; unclear why sign-flipping is the principled approach for negative guidance
Unresolved fundamental trade-off: Method shifts but does not solve the inherent positive-negative adherence trade-off (Figure 8); no clear practical guidance for hyperparameter selection
Limited scope: Primarily validated on SD 3.5; Wan 2.1 testing is brief; video generation underdeveloped; method requires architectural modifications for some models

Potential evaluation bias: NAG hyperparameters explicitly tuned while baseline tuning effort unclear; some baselines reimplemented introducing implementation risk; MLLM may exhibit different systematic biases across methods
Missing human evaluation validation: Quality claims based on HPSV2/ImageReward metrics that don't account for negative prompts, making the actual user-perceived improvements unclear

strengths: Addresses a practically important problem—negative guidance in few-step models with limited existing solutions
Comprehensive experimental study with multiple baselines, trade-off analysis, and ablation studies
Demonstrates computational efficiency improvements over CFG while maintaining comparable or better negative guidance
Good visual demonstrations of the method's ability to suppress unwanted objects (Figures 4 and 7)
Provides sufficient implementation details for potential reproduction
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Sign-flipping for negative guidance is acknowledged as similar to existing NASA/NAG methods; the incremental difference (adaptive vs. fixed scales) lacks clear technical justification
Critical evaluation limitation: Heavy reliance on MMLU-based metrics without human evaluation, despite acknowledging MMLU's unreliability when subtle unwanted elements are present
No statistical rigor: Claims of 'significant improvement' lack confidence intervals, significance tests, or rigorous comparative statistics
Trade-off analysis reveals non-dominance: Figure 8 shows VSF does not uniformly outperform baselines at all operating points; guidance on method selection is absent
Technical formulation lacks motivation: Equation 6's specific form and its theoretical advantages over NASA are not rigorously justified
Hyperparameter tuning bias: Manual tuning of NAG parameters with emphasis on quality could bias comparisons; unclear if consistent across trade-off studies
Limited scope: Evaluation primarily on SD3.5 Turbo with only 200 prompts; Wan 2.1 results lack quantitative analysis; no systematic failure case analysis
Unclear design choices: Several components (padding removal, attention masking, WEF variant) lack clear motivation and isolated impact demonstration
Computational overhead not negligible: ~40% runtime increase (3.0s vs 2.14s) contradicts 'efficient' positioning; no CFG runtime comparison provided
Reproducibility concerns: No code availability mentioned, exact prompt construction unclear, external baseline comparisons use different inference settings

strengths: Elegant and practical method that enables negative guidance in few-step models with minimal computational overhead and no retraining required
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including extensive ablations, trade-off curves, and systematic component analysis across multiple datasets
Significant computational efficiency advantages over baselines (3s vs 25.5s for NASA on SD3.5), making the method practically deployable
Clear technical presentation with transparent mathematical formulation (Equations 1-6) and effective visualizations of attention mechanisms
Thorough problem analysis addressing architectural challenges (attention bias, padding issues) with targeted solutions for MMDiT-style models
Practical value demonstrated through integration with existing models without modification, immediately applicable to practitioners
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on MLLM-based evaluation metrics, which authors acknowledge can be flawed; Figure 6 demonstrates severely distorted images receiving quality scores ~70, suggesting the metric does not reliably capture perceptual quality

Trade-off curves show quality degradation at higher negative scores (Figure 8), but claims of 'broader operational range' and 'universal superiority' are not clearly supported; unclear when practitioners should choose VSF over NAG

Limited fundamental novelty—core idea of sign-flipping for negative guidance builds directly on prior work (Koulischer et al., Schramowski et al.); contribution is primarily engineering-focused rather than conceptual
Generalization constraints including failure with Flux Schnell architecture (Section 4.10) and limited evaluation beyond SD3.5; specific modifications needed for MMDiT suggest architecture-dependence
Hyperparameter tuning without principled guidance (σ=11, ο=0.5, τ=5 manually selected); no clear strategy for adapting parameters to new models or datasets

Baseline comparison concerns: NASA reimplemented from NAG codebase rather than original code (unavailable), raising fairness questions; incomplete comparison with other recent methods (GPT-4o, Janus-4o, Qwen-Image)
Incomplete analysis of failure modes and trade-offs; Appendix A.1 shows failures with unnatural physics and missing elements but lacks systematic characterization of success/failure conditions

Architectural modifications (masking, duplication, padding removal) appear as model-specific patches; simpler Whole Embedding Flip performs comparably but receives less emphasis, suggesting unclear motivation for complexity

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine limitation of existing negative guidance methods in few-step models with clear examples and compelling motivation

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including systematic trade-off analysis (hypersweep with 66+ runs for VSF and 287 for NAG), ablation studies, and testing across multiple models (SD 3.5, Wan, Flux)
Strong empirical results showing significant improvements in negative score (0.545 vs 0.220-0.380) while maintaining image quality (0.952) and achieving faster runtime
Simple, elegant, and practical method with minimal computational overhead that integrates with diverse architectures without major modifications
Thorough supplementary materials including mathematical proofs, detailed implementation (pseudocode), ablation studies, qualitative analysis, and human validation
Good reproducibility practices: code and dataset release commitment, detailed hyperparameters, and transparent discussion of limitations
Thoughtful technical design including attention masking to prevent side effects, attention bias for quality preservation, and padding token handling
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core contribution is incremental extension of Koulischer et al. (2025) to token-level modulation, with straightforward application of sign-flipping

Significant evaluation concerns: heavy reliance on LLaMA-4 Maverick MLLM which has known limitations (Figure 9 shows poor correlation with human judgment); human validation only on 10 prompts with 2 seeds is insufficient for robust claims

Dataset limitations: NeqGenBench contains only 200 ChatGPT-generated prompts (×2 seeds), small size and potential bias; 'challenging' aspect (intentional positive-negative relationships) acknowledged as unrealistic
Missing recent baseline comparisons: Ban et al. (2024) on dynamic negative guidance and other recent methods not evaluated; external baselines in Table 1 use different training conditions
Narrow evaluation scope: primarily focuses on object removal; limited exploration of other negative guidance scenarios; generalization to full diffusion pipelines and non-few-step models unclear

Hyperparameter sensitivity not fully addressed: requires tuning both σ and β; different hyperparameters for different quality targets (contradicts 'only one main hyperparameter' claim); limited guidance for new datasets/models
Insufficient failure case analysis: Appendix L shows failures but lacks principled understanding of failure modes or systematic approach to predict when method will fail
Limited ablation coverage: minimal testing of mask design variants, no systematic exploration of different attention mechanisms, limited architectural diversity
